title: Spring MVC: controllers, DTOs and validation (Bean Validation)

videos.script: Since lesson 4 the bookshop has been a web server. It has never answered a question. Every request gets a 404. {{silent}} Lesson 5 gave it a service and three books, and nothing outside can reach them. This lesson opens the door. {{door}} You write a controller: a class whose methods are labelled with the requests they answer. You never read a socket or parse a header. {{controller}} One servlet receives every request. It finds your method, converts the path and the body, and writes what you return as JSON. {{dispatcher}} Then the records that travel on the wire, and why they are not the domain's. {{dtos}} Clients get to create books. And the bookshop happily stores one with an empty title and a price below zero. {{junk}} Bean Validation closes that gap. The rules go on the request, and Spring checks them before your method runs. {{rules}} The last rule is your own: the check digit at the end of every ISBN. {{isbn}}
